issues.q: When is borrowed money added to the Zakat base?
issues.old: Under the 1440H Regulations (Art 4(3)) debts were added if they were long-term or lasted 354 days or more across the year, pro rata by days, and only up to the total deductions. Committees applied the same 'full lunar year (hawl)' idea to earlier years.
issues.take: From 2024 the test is the balance-sheet classification: non-current liabilities are added, but only in proportion to the non-current assets actually deducted; current liabilities are added only when a current asset is deducted. Partner loans follow Article 30.
issues.h: For 2019-2023 audits, rebuild the loan timeline by days; for 2024+, start from the balance-sheet classification.

issues.t: Adjusted net profit and the minimum base
issues.q: Is the year's adjusted profit always Zakat-able?
issues.old: The 1440H Regulations (Art 6(1)) said the base cannot be lower than the adjusted net profit. Committees held that the whole adjusted profit is Zakat-able as a return on capital, whether or not a lunar year has passed or it was distributed.
issues.take: Article 27 now spells out the floor: if the base falls below adjusted profit, the base is the lower of adjusted profit or the undeducted assets plus profit adjustments. Article 28 adds a ceiling of year-end equity plus adjustments.
issues.h: Run three numbers every year: the computed base, the floor and the ceiling.

issues.q: Which balance of retained earnings counts?
issues.old: Under 1440H (Art 4(4)-(5)) the opening balances of reserves and retained earnings were added, reflecting the hawl idea; committees applied that and allowed actuarial losses to be deducted from retained earnings.
issues.take: From 2024 equity is taken at the year-end balance, and accumulated losses reduce equity (Article 39) - there is no separate opening-balance test.
issues.h: Old years: opening balances. New years: closing equity.

issues.q: Which investments come out of the base?
issues.old: Under 1440H (Art 5(4)-(5)) non-trading investments in Saudi entities registered for Zakat were deducted; foreign ones only with Zakat paid on them through a Saudi CPA certificate. Committees refused deductions for items such as sukuk and Islamic deposits abroad.
issues.take: Articles 42-47 keep the non-trading and registration tests, add funds and companies not subject to Zakat, and Article 55 lets investors deduct sukuk only where the issuer treats them as capital.
issues.h: For every investment, write down: non-current? non-trading? investee pays Zakat in KSA or certificate in hand?

issues.old: Under 1440H provisions were added at the opening balance less amounts used (Art 4(6)), and provisions formed in the year were not deductible expenses (Art 9(5)). Committees treated provisions used for related-party debts as non-deductible.
issues.take: From 2024 provisions are added at the closing balance as equity, except end-of-service and leave provisions, which are non-current liabilities. Bad debts with related parties are still not deductible (Article 65).
issues.h: Split provisions into 'really ours' (equity) and 'owed to staff' (liabilities).

issues.t: Time limits for reopening a year
issues.old: Income tax: 5 years from the filing deadline, 10 years in failure cases (Law Art 65). Zakat 1440H: 5 years, 10 years for arithmetic errors or failure cases (Arts 21-22). Committees treat the time bar as a right of the payer that ZATCA cannot waive for itself.
issues.take: Zakat 1445H Article 106 keeps 5 and 10 years and adds no limit for intentional evasion. The 2023 draft procedures law would shorten the normal period to 3 years - not yet law.
issues.h: Keep a year-by-year 'time-bar date' column in your compliance tracker.

issues.q: Does a Saudi branch withhold tax when it pays its head office?
issues.old: Law Art 4 treats a licensed branch as a PE, and Law Art 68 requires a PE to withhold on payments to non-residents. Committees have upheld WHT on branch payments to head office for services.
issues.take: A branch is a separate withholding agent: classify each head-office charge and withhold at the Article 63 rate, subject to treaty relief.
issues.h: Head-office recharge = payment to a non-resident: run the WHT checklist.

issues.q: Is the 1% delay fine always due on additional tax?
issues.old: Law Art 77 and Bylaws Art 68 impose 1% for each 30 days of delay. Committees have cancelled the fine where the tax itself is cancelled, and some decisions excused it where the dispute was a genuine technical or interpretive one.
issues.take: Fine relief depends on the facts and the committee; it is safest to pay disputed tax (or the required percentage) and argue the fine separately.
issues.h: Argue the fine as its own item in every objection.

issues.q: Is a payment for software a royalty?
issues.old: Law Art 68 and Bylaws Art 63 tax royalties at 15%. Committees look at what was really paid for - the right to use intellectual property versus buying a product - and at who really benefits from the payment.
issues.take: Classify on substance: a right to copy, modify or exploit points to royalty; a simple licence to use a product may not. Check the treaty definition too.
issues.h: Read the licence terms before applying a WHT rate.

issues.q: Will ZATCA accept my benchmarking set?
issues.old: Law Art 63 lets ZATCA adjust related-party prices to arm's length (detailed rules are in the separate Transfer Pricing Bylaws). Committees require comparables to be shown as independent with adequate financial data, and recalculate when the range moves.
issues.take: Document independence screens and data quality for every comparable - an excluded comparable can move the interquartile range and the penalties.
issues.h: Keep the screening evidence with the benchmark, not just the final set.

meta.status: Drafts only. ZATCA published both drafts for public consultation on the Istitlaa portal from 25 October to 25 December 2023. As at 25 November 2026 we found no announcement that either has been approved, so the current Law, Bylaws and Zakat Regulations still apply.
meta.why: The official draft texts could not be downloaded from Istitlaa for this library, so each line below is taken from the named firm's public summary of the drafts. Read the draft itself before relying on any point.

itl.d: A new Income Tax Law would replace the 2004 Law. It would take effect 90 days after publication in the Official Gazette, for tax years starting after that date; new implementing regulations would follow.

New tests are proposed for individuals - EY reports presence of 90 days in a tax year together with 270 days over the three prior years; KPMG reports a test for holders of a residence permit present 30 days within 365 days.
An explicit services PE: services by a non-resident in KSA lasting 30 days within any 12-month period would create a PE.

Where a non-resident with a Saudi PE also sells directly to Saudi customers in the PE's line of business, the profit can be attributed to the PE unless there is a proper business reason (a limited force-of-attraction rule).
Gains on an indirect sale of shares in a Saudi entity and services performed remotely by electronic means would be Saudi-source.

WHT on payments to non-residents would be: rent, dividends (including bonus shares) and interest on related-party debt 5%; all services 10% (today 5%, 15% or 20% depending on the service); 20% on interest, dividends, rent, services and royalties paid to residents of preferential tax regimes. Salaries, board members' remuneration and payments to transparent entities would not be subject to WHT.
Interest deductions would be capped at 30% of taxable profit.
Carried-forward losses could be used up to the full taxable profit of the year (today capped at 25%).
Tax depreciation would move to the straight-line method; gains on depreciable assets could be deferred into a reinvestment reserve, subject to conditions.

Gains and losses on qualifying mergers and demergers, and gains on certain intra-group share transfers by non-resident capital companies to a resident company, would be excluded from tax, subject to conditions.
Income of funds would be taxed in the hands of partners, shareholders or unitholders, and partnership taxation would change.
Tax paid abroad could be credited against Saudi tax, subject to conditions. There is no general foreign tax credit in the current Law.

Hybrid-mismatch rules for instruments between related persons, a preferential-tax-regime concept, a wider related-person definition aligned with the transfer pricing rules, and corresponding-adjustment rules.

Detailed rules for non-Saudi individuals carrying on business independently and regularly; salaries and similar pay excluded from taxable income subject to conditions; simpler methods for micro-enterprises.

ztpl.d: A single Zakat and Tax Procedures Law would hold the administrative rules - registration, returns, examination, assessment, collection and penalties - now spread across the Income Tax Law, its Bylaws and the Zakat Regulations.
A self-assessment system for returns filed within the set time limits.
Shorter: 3 years from the end of the calendar year in which the filing deadline expired (today 5 years from the filing deadline).
Refund requests within 3 years from the end of the calendar year in which the return was filed (today 5 years).
A new, generally higher, penalty structure.
ZATCA could send notices in English or another language, at its discretion.

glossary: An Islamic levy of 2.5% a year on Zakat-able wealth. In KSA it is collected by ZATCA from Saudi and GCC owners' share of a business.
A 20% tax on the foreign (non-Saudi, non-GCC) share of a resident company's profit, on non-residents' PEs and on some other persons.
The Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority - formerly GAZT (General Authority of Zakat and Tax) and before that DZIT.
The General Secretariat of Zakat, Tax and Customs Committees - runs the committees that decide disputes with ZATCA and publishes their decisions and principles.

Your financial year for Zakat - Hijri or Gregorian, long or short.
A lunar year of about 354 days. A Gregorian year is longer, so the Zakat rate is scaled up by days.
The passing of a full lunar year over wealth - the classic condition for Zakat, behind the old 354-day loan test.
The amount Zakat is charged on: what is added (equity, certain liabilities, profit adjustments) less what is deducted (long-term assets and qualifying investments).
Items put into the Zakat base - equity and equivalents, qualifying liabilities and profit adjustments.
Items taken out of the base - net fixed assets, intangibles, qualifying investments, materials not for sale and others.
Book profit after the add-backs and deductions the Zakat rules require.
The rule that stops the base falling below adjusted profit (with a cap at undeducted assets plus adjustments).
The rule that caps the base at year-end equity plus profit adjustments.
Capital, reserves, retained earnings and items treated like them, such as some provisions, partner loans and declared dividends.
Debts due after more than a year, plus items such as end-of-service and leave provisions, deferred tax and lease liabilities.
An estimate of Zakat or tax made by ZATCA when books, returns or documents are missing or unreliable.
The formula basis for small payers without statutory accounts: base = sales ÷ 8 + 15% of sales, minimum Zakat SAR 500.
A fixed place or person through which a non-resident does business in KSA; its profit is taxed here.
A person meeting the residence tests - for companies, formed in KSA or managed from KSA.
Tax the Saudi payer deducts from payments to non-residents and pays to ZATCA by the 10th of the next month.
A payment for the right to use intellectual property, know-how or equipment - WHT 15%.
Payments under management contracts, such as hotel or ship management - WHT 20%.
Technical, scientific, engineering, consulting or supervisory services - WHT 5%.
Three income tax instalments during the year (months 6, 9 and 12), each 25% of last year's tax less last year's WHT; not needed if that figure is below SAR 500,000.
1% of unpaid tax for each 30 days of delay.
The fine for not filing on time: the higher of 1% of revenue (max SAR 20,000) or 5%-25% of unpaid tax.
ZATCA's decision accepting or amending your return.
Your formal challenge to a ZATCA decision - first to ZATCA, then to the GSTC committees.
The period within which ZATCA may assess or reopen a year - normally 5 years.
The price independent parties would agree - the test for related-party dealings.
A person who can control or influence the other, or under common control.
One Zakat return for a holding company and its 100%-owned subsidiaries.
Banks, finance companies and financing funds - Zakat base under special rules.
The Minister's detailed rules under the Income Tax Law (MR 1535 of 1425H, as amended).
A decision of the Minister of Finance - used to issue and amend the Bylaws and the Zakat Regulations.
The instrument that issues or amends a Law, such as Royal Decree M/1 of 1425H for the Income Tax Law.
